translations.idiomatic: The dragon rose in the northern capital, and righteous wind spread over the nine domains;

sentences.zh: 鳳翔天域，則威聲格於八表。

translations.literal: the phoenix soared in the heavenly realm, then awesome renown reached the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: the phoenix soared in the celestial realm, and his awesome name reached the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 屬奸雄鼎峙之秋，群凶嶽立之際，昧旦臨朝，日旰忘膳，運籌命將，舉無遺策。

translations.literal: In the season when treacherous heroes stood like cauldrons and many villains rose like peaks, he attended court before dawn and forgot his meal at dusk, deploying stratagems and appointing generals, and in every move left no plan unused.
translations.idiomatic: In the season when rival strongmen stood like cauldrons and enemies rose like mountain peaks, he held court before dawn and forgot his meal at dusk, laying stratagems and appointing commanders until no plan remained unused.

sentences.zh: 親禦六戎，則有征無戰。

translations.literal: When he personally commanded the six armies, there was campaigning but no fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When he personally led the six armies, campaigns ended without battle.

sentences.zh: 故偽秦以三世之資，喪魂于關、隴；

translations.literal: Therefore the false Qin, with the resources of three generations, lost its soul at Pass and Long;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the false Qin, with three generations of strength behind it, lost heart at Pass and Long;

sentences.zh: 河源望旗而委質，北虜欽風而納款。

translations.literal: the River Source submitted on sight of the banners, and the northern barbarians, awed by his wind, tendered allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: the River Source surrendered at sight of his banners, and the northern tribes, awed by his renown, offered submission.

sentences.zh: 德音著於柔服，威刑彰於伐叛，文教與武功並宣，俎豆與干戈俱運。

translations.literal: Virtuous fame showed among those who yielded, awesome punishment shone on those who rebelled; civil teaching and martial achievement were proclaimed together, sacrificial vessels and weapons moved in the same course.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue was known among those who submitted; his punishment blazed against rebels. Civil teaching and martial achievement were proclaimed together; ritual vessels and weapons of war moved in one course.

sentences.zh: 五稔之間，道風弘著，暨乎七載而王猷允洽。

translations.literal: Within five harvest-years the Way's wind was greatly displayed; by the seventh year the royal design was fully harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Within five years the Way's influence stood clear; by the seventh year the royal design was fully achieved.

sentences.zh: 乃遠惟周文，啟經始之基；

translations.literal: Then looking far to King Wen of Zhou, he opened the foundation of beginning;
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to King Wen of Zhou, he opened the foundation of a new beginning;

sentences.zh: 近詳山川，究形勝之地，遂營起都城，開建京邑。

translations.literal: examining near the mountains and rivers, he investigated the terrain of strategic advantage, and thereupon raised the capital city and opened the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: and surveying the mountains and rivers nearby, he studied the ground of strategic advantage. Thereupon he raised a capital and opened an imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 背名山而面洪流，左河津而右重塞。

translations.literal: Backed by famous mountains and facing rushing streams, with the river crossing on the left and layered passes on the right.
translations.idiomatic: It backed on famous peaks and faced rushing waters, with the river crossing to the left and layered passes to the right.

sentences.zh: 高隅隱日，崇墉際雲，石郭天池，周綿千里。

translations.literal: High corners hid the sun, lofty walls met the clouds; stone walls and heavenly moats encircled a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Its high corners blocked out the sun; its towering walls touched the clouds. Stone ramparts and heavenly moats ran a thousand li around.

sentences.zh: 其為獨守之形，險絕之狀，固以遠邁於咸陽，超美于周洛，若乃廣五郊之義，尊七廟之制，崇左社之規，建右稷之禮，禦太一以繕明堂，模帝坐而營路寢，閶闔披霄而山亭，象魏排虛而岳峙，華林靈沼，崇台秘室，通房連閣，馳道苑園，可以陰映萬邦，光覆四海，莫不鬱然並建，森然畢備，若紫微之帶皇穹，閬風之跨后土。

translations.literal: As a form for holding alone, in shape of utmost peril, it already far surpassed Xianyang and excelled Zhou and Luo. As for extending the rites of the five suburbs, honoring the system of the seven temples, revering the rule of the left altar of soil, establishing the ceremony of the right altar of grain, repairing the Bright Hall to honor Grand Unity, modeling the imperial seat to build the road chamber—the Gate of Heaven pierced the sky like a mountain pavilion, the Gate of Virtue rose void like a peak; the Flowery Forest and Spirit Pool, lofty terraces and hidden chambers, connecting rooms and linked pavilions, imperial roads and park gardens—all could cast shadow over myriad states and spread light over the four seas. None failed to rise together in splendor and stand complete in array, like the Purple Palace girdling the imperial vault, or Langfeng spanning the rear earth.
translations.idiomatic: In form it was a fortress apart, in shape utterly impregnable—already far beyond Xianyang, already surpassing Zhou and Luoyang. It extended the rites of the five suburbs, honored the system of the seven temples, observed the rule of the left altar of soil, established the ceremony of the right altar of grain, repaired the Bright Hall for Grand Unity, modeled the imperial seat in the road chamber. The Gate of Heaven pierced the sky like a mountain pavilion; the Gate of Virtue rose empty as a peak. Flowery Forest and Spirit Pool, lofty terraces and hidden chambers, linked rooms and connecting halls, imperial roads and park gardens—all could cast shadow over myriad states and spread light across the four seas. Each rose in splendor and stood complete, like the Purple Palace girdling the vault of heaven, like Langfeng spanning the rear earth.

sentences.zh: 然宰司鼎臣，群黎士庶，僉以為重威之式，有闕前王。

translations.literal: Yet the chief ministers and the masses of officials and common people all considered that in the form of heavy authority something was lacking compared with former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet chief ministers, officials, and common people alike judged that in the outward form of imperial majesty something still fell short of former kings.

sentences.zh: 於是延王爾之奇工，命班輸之妙匠，搜文梓于鄧林，采繡石于恆嶽，九域貢以金銀，八方獻其瑰寶，親運神奇，參制規矩，營離宮於露寢之南，起別殿于永安之北。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned the wondrous craftsmen of Wang Er, commanded the subtle artisans of Ban Shu, sought patterned catalpa in the Deng Forest, gathered brocade stone on Mount Heng, had the nine regions tribute gold and silver, had the eight directions present their rare treasures, personally applied divine wonder, jointly set the compass and square, built a detached palace south of the dew chamber, and raised a separate hall north of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he summoned the wondrous craftsmen of Wang Er and commanded the subtle artisans of Ban Shu. He sought patterned catalpa in the Deng Forest and gathered brocade stone on Mount Heng. The nine regions sent gold and silver; the eight directions offered rare treasures. He himself applied divine craft and jointly set compass and square. He built a detached palace south of the dew chamber and raised a separate hall north of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 高構千尋，崇基萬仞。

translations.literal: Lofty structures a thousand fathoms, towering foundations ten thousand ren.
translations.idiomatic: Its lofty structures rose a thousand fathoms; its towering foundations stood ten thousand ren high.

sentences.zh: 玄棟鏤榥，若騰虹之揚眉；

translations.literal: Dark pillars carved with rafters, like a soaring rainbow lifting its brow;
translations.idiomatic: Dark pillars carved with rafters rose like a soaring rainbow lifting its brow;

sentences.zh: 飛簷舒咢，似翔鵬之矯翼。

translations.literal: flying eaves extending their beaks, like a soaring peng spreading its wings.
translations.idiomatic: flying eaves thrust out their beaks like a soaring peng spreading its wings.

sentences.zh: 二序啟矣，而五時之坐開；

translations.literal: The two wings opened, and the seats of the five seasons were unveiled;
translations.idiomatic: The two wings opened, and the seats of the five seasons were unveiled;

sentences.zh: 四隅陳設，而一禦之位建。

translations.literal: the four corners were arrayed, and the one imperial seat was established.
translations.idiomatic: the four corners were set in array, and the single imperial seat was established.

sentences.zh: 溫宮膠葛，涼殿崢嶸，絡以隋珠，綷以金鏡，雖曦望互升於表，而中無晝夜之殊；

translations.literal: Warm chambers stretched in vast reach, cool halls rose steep and lofty, laced with Sui pearls, woven with gold mirrors—though dawn and dusk alternated outside, within there was no difference of day and night;
translations.idiomatic: Warm chambers stretched vast and far; cool halls rose steep and lofty, laced with Sui pearls and woven with gold mirrors. Though dawn and dusk changed outside, within there was neither day nor night;

sentences.zh: 陰陽迭更於外，而內無寒暑之別。

translations.literal: yin and yang alternated without, yet within there was no distinction of cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: though yin and yang shifted without, within there was no difference of cold and heat.

sentences.zh: 故善目者不能為其名，博辯者不能究其稱，斯蓋神明之所規模，非人工之所經制。

translations.literal: Therefore even keen-eyed men could not name it, and eloquent debaters could not exhaust its title—this was a design of the numinous, not a work human hands could measure.
translations.idiomatic: Keen-eyed men could not name it; eloquent debaters could not exhaust its titles. This was a design of the numinous, not a work human hands could measure.

sentences.zh: 若乃尋名以求類，蹤狀以效真，據質以究名，形疑妙出，雖如來、須彌之寶塔，帝釋、忉利之神宮，尚未足以喻其麗，方其飾矣。

translations.literal: If one sought categories by name, traced form to test truth, examined substance to reach name, and form seemed to issue from wonder—even the treasure pagoda of Tathagata and Mount Sumeru, the divine palace of Shakra in Trayastrimsa, would not suffice to match its beauty when ornamented thus.
translations.idiomatic: If one sought likeness by name, traced form to test truth, and weighed substance against title until form seemed to issue from wonder—even the treasure pagoda of the Tathagata on Mount Sumeru, even the divine palace of Shakra in Trayastrimsa, would not suffice to match its splendor once adorned thus.

sentences.zh: 昔周宣考室而詠于詩人，閟宮有侐而頌聲是作。

translations.literal: Of old King Xuan of Zhou examined his chamber and the poets sang; the Closed Palace had its spaciousness and eulogy arose.
translations.idiomatic: Of old King Xuan of Zhou examined his chamber and poets sang of it; the Closed Palace had its spaciousness and eulogy arose.

sentences.zh: 況乃太微肇制，清都啟建，軌一文昌，舊章唯始，咸秩百神，賓享萬國，群生開其耳目，天下詠其來蘇，亦何得不播之管弦，刊之金石哉！

translations.literal: How much more when the Grand Microcosm first took form, the Pure Capital was opened and built, the track unified at the Palace of Literary Glory, old statutes had their beginning, all ranks of spirits were ordered, myriad states were received as guests—the masses opened their ears and eyes, and under heaven they sang of returning life—how could one fail to spread it in string and pipe, or carve it in metal and stone!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the Grand Microcosm first took form, when the Pure Capital was opened and built, when the track was unified at the Palace of Literary Glory and old statutes had their beginning, when all ranks of spirits were ordered and myriad states received as guests, when the people opened their ears and eyes and all under heaven sang of returning life—how could one fail to spread it in string and pipe, or carve it in metal and stone!

sentences.zh: 乃樹銘都邑，敷贊碩美，俾皇風振于來葉，聖庸垂乎不朽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set up an inscription in the capital, spread and praised its great beauty, so that imperial wind would stir future ages and sacred merit would hang immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he set up an inscription in the capital, spread and praised its great beauty, so that imperial wind would stir future ages and sacred merit would hang immortal.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: The words say:
translations.idiomatic: The words say:

sentences.zh: 於赫靈祚，配乾比靈斯。

translations.literal: Oh, the numinous fortune—matching heaven, rivaling the numinous.
translations.idiomatic: Oh, the numinous fortune—matching heaven, rivaling the divine.

sentences.zh: 巍巍大禹，堂堂聖功。

translations.literal: Vast is Yu the Great, lofty his sacred achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Vast is Yu the Great; lofty his sacred achievement.

sentences.zh: 仁被蒼生，德格玄穹。

translations.literal: Benevolence covered the black-haired people, virtue reached the dark vault.
translations.idiomatic: His benevolence covered the black-haired people; his virtue reached the dark vault.

sentences.zh: 帝錫玄珪，揖讓受終。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed the dark jade tablet; he yielded and received the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor bestowed the dark jade tablet; he yielded and received the end.

sentences.zh: 哲王繼軌，光闡徽風。

translations.literal: Wise kings followed in the track, brightly extending fine wind.
translations.idiomatic: Wise kings followed in the track, brightly extending fine policy.

sentences.zh: 道無常夷，數或不競。

translations.literal: The Way is not always level, and the times sometimes do not contend.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is not always level; fate sometimes turns against us.

sentences.zh: 金精南邁，天輝北映。

translations.literal: The golden essence moved south, heavenly radiance mirrored north.
translations.idiomatic: The golden essence moved south; heavenly radiance mirrored north.

sentences.zh: 靈祉逾昌，世葉彌盛。

translations.literal: Numinous blessing grew ever fuller, generation and branch ever more flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Numinous blessing grew ever fuller; generation and branch ever more flourishing.

sentences.zh: 惟祖惟父，克廣休命。

translations.literal: Forefathers and fathers alike broadened the fair mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Forefathers and fathers alike broadened the fair mandate.

sentences.zh: 如彼日月，連光接鏡。

translations.literal: Like sun and moon, their light joined and their mirrors met.
translations.idiomatic: Like sun and moon, their light joined and their mirrors met.

sentences.zh: 玄符瑞德，乾運有歸。

translations.literal: Dark talisman, auspicious virtue—heaven's course had its return.
translations.idiomatic: Dark omen, auspicious virtue—heaven's course had its return.

sentences.zh: 誕鐘我後，應圖龍飛。

translations.literal: Born at the bell of our latter age, he answered the chart and the dragon flew.
translations.idiomatic: Born at the bell of our latter age, he answered the chart and the dragon flew.

sentences.zh: 落落神武，恢恢聖姿。

translations.literal: Lofty in divine martial bearing, vast in sacred mien.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty in divine martial bearing, vast in sacred mien.

sentences.zh: 名教內敷，群妖外夷。

translations.literal: Within, name and teaching spread; without, many demons were leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Within, name and teaching spread; without, many demons were leveled.

sentences.zh: 化光四表，威截九圍。

translations.literal: Transforming light to the four quarters, awesome reach cutting the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming light to the four quarters, awesome reach cutting the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 封畿之制，王者常經。

translations.literal: The system of the sealed frontier—the constant canon of kings.
translations.idiomatic: The system of the sealed frontier—the constant canon of kings.

sentences.zh: 乃延輸、爾，肇建帝京。

translations.literal: Then he summoned Shu and Er and first raised the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Then he summoned Shu and Er and first raised the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 土苞上壤，地跨勝形。

translations.literal: Earth wrapped the upper soil, land crossed victorious form.
translations.idiomatic: Earth wrapped the upper soil; land crossed victorious ground.

sentences.zh: 庶人子來，不日而成。

translations.literal: Common people came like sons; it was completed not in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Common people came like sons; it was completed not in a day.

sentences.zh: 崇台霄峙，秀闕雲亭。

translations.literal: Lofty terraces stood like peaks, elegant gates rose like cloud pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty terraces stood like peaks; elegant gates rose like cloud pavilions.

sentences.zh: 千榭連隅，萬閣接屏。

translations.literal: A thousand pavilions linked corner to corner, ten thousand halls joined screen to screen.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand pavilions linked corner to corner; ten thousand halls joined screen to screen.

sentences.zh: 晃若晨曦，昭若列星。

translations.literal: Bright as dawn light, clear as ranged stars.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as dawn light, clear as ranged stars.

sentences.zh: 離宮既作，別宇雲施。

translations.literal: The detached palace was made, separate halls spread like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The detached palace was made; separate halls spread like clouds.

sentences.zh: 爰構崇明，仰准乾儀。

translations.literal: He then built Chongming, looking up to the standard of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He then built Chongming, looking up to the standard of Qian.

sentences.zh: 懸薨風閱，飛軒雲垂。

translations.literal: Suspended rafters wind-swept, flying galleries cloud-hung.
translations.idiomatic: Suspended rafters wind-swept; flying galleries cloud-hung.

sentences.zh: 溫室嵯峨，層城參差。

translations.literal: Warm chambers towered steep, layered walls rose uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Warm chambers towered steep; layered walls rose uneven.

sentences.zh: 楹雕虯獸，節鏤龍螭。

translations.literal: Pillars carved with horned beasts, nodes inlaid with dragon and wyrm.
translations.idiomatic: Pillars carved with horned beasts; nodes inlaid with dragon and wyrm.

sentences.zh: 瑩以寶璞，飾以珍奇。

translations.literal: Polished with precious jade, adorned with rare wonders.
translations.idiomatic: Polished with precious jade, adorned with rare wonders.

sentences.zh: 稱因褒著，名由實揚。

translations.literal: Title follows praise in display, name rises from substance in renown.
translations.idiomatic: Title follows praise in display; name rises from substance in renown.

sentences.zh: 偉哉皇室，盛矣厥章！

translations.literal: Great the imperial house, flourishing its statutes!
translations.idiomatic: Great the imperial house, flourishing its statutes!

sentences.zh: 義高靈台，美隆未央。

translations.literal: Righteousness higher than the Spirit Tower, beauty greater than Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness higher than the Spirit Tower, beauty greater than Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 邁軌三五，貽則霸王。

translations.literal: Surpassing the tracks of the Three and Five, bequeathing models to hegemons and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Surpassing the tracks of the Three and Five, bequeathing models to hegemons and kings.

sentences.zh: 永世垂節，億載彌光。

translations.literal: Forever hanging its standard, for a hundred million years spreading its light.
translations.idiomatic: Forever hanging its standard, for a hundred million years spreading its light.

sentences.zh: 其秘書監胡義周之辭也。

translations.literal: This was the composition of Secretary Director Hu Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: This was the composition of Secretary Director Hu Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 名其南門曰朝宋門，東門曰招魏門，西門曰服涼門，北門曰平朔門。

translations.literal: He named the southern gate Gate of Court to Song, the eastern gate Gate of Summoning Wei, the western gate Gate of Submitting to Liang, and the northern gate Gate of Pacifying Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: He named the southern gate Gate of Court to Song, the eastern gate Gate of Summoning Wei, the western gate Gate of Submitting to Liang, and the northern gate Gate of Pacifying Shuo.

sentences.zh: 追尊其高祖訓兒曰元皇帝，曾祖武曰景皇帝，祖豹子曰宣皇帝，父衛辰曰桓皇帝，廟號太祖，母苻氏曰桓文皇后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his great-grandfather Xun'er as Emperor Yuan, his grandfather Wu as Emperor Jing, his grandfather Baozi as Emperor Xuan, his father Wei Chen as Emperor Huan, with temple title Taizu, and his mother Lady Fu as Empress Dowager Huanwen.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his great-grandfather Xun'er as Emperor Yuan, his grandfather Wu as Emperor Jing, his grandfather Baozi as Emperor Xuan, his father Wei Chen as Emperor Huan, with temple title Taizu, and his mother Lady Fu as Empress Dowager Huanwen.

sentences.zh: 勃勃性凶暴好殺，無順守之規。

translations.literal: Bobo by nature was fierce, violent, and fond of killing, with no rule of orderly preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo was by nature fierce, violent, and fond of killing, with no thought of orderly rule.

sentences.zh: 常居城上，置弓劍於側，有所嫌忿，便手自殺之，群臣忤視者毀其目，笑者決其脣，諫者謂之誹謗，先截其舌而後斬之。

translations.literal: He constantly sat atop the city wall with bow and sword at his side; whenever he felt resentment, he would personally kill the man. Ministers who looked at him askance had their eyes destroyed; those who laughed had their lips cut; remonstrators he called slanderers—first he cut out their tongues, then beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly sat atop the city wall with bow and sword at his side. Whenever resentment stirred in him, he killed with his own hand. Ministers who looked at him askance had their eyes put out; those who laughed had their lips cut; remonstrators he called slanderers—first he cut out their tongues, then beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 夷夏囂然，人無生賴。

translations.literal: Barbarian and Chinese alike were in uproar, and men had no means to live.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian and Chinese alike were in uproar, and men had no means to live.

sentences.zh: 在位十三年而宋受禪，以宋元嘉二年死。

translations.literal: He reigned thirteen years, and when Song received the Mandate, he died in the second year of Song Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned thirteen years. When Song received the Mandate, he died in the second year of Song Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 子昌嗣偽位，尋為魏所擒。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded to the false throne and was soon captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded to the false throne and was soon captured by Wei.

sentences.zh: 弟定僭號於平涼，遂為魏所滅。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ding usurped title at Pingliang and was thereupon destroyed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ding usurped title at Pingliang and was thereupon destroyed by Wei.

sentences.zh: 自勃勃至定，凡二十有六載而亡。

translations.literal: From Bobo to Ding, in all twenty-six years and then extinction.
translations.idiomatic: From Bobo to Ding, twenty-six years in all—and then extinction.

sentences.zh: 【評贊】

translations.literal: 【Commentary and Praise】
translations.idiomatic: 【Commentary and Praise】

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：赫連勃勃犬熏醜種類，入居邊宇，屬中壤分崩，緣間肆慝，控弦鳴鏑，據有朔方。

translations.literal: The historian says: Helian Bobo was a dog-stench, ugly breed who entered and settled in the frontier region. When the central lands split apart, he seized the interval to unleash wickedness, sounded bow and whistling arrow, and held Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Helian Bobo was of a foul, barbarian breed who settled the frontier marches. When the central realm split apart, he seized the opening to unleash wickedness, strung his bow and sounded his whistling arrow, and held Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 遂乃法玄象以開宮，擬神京而建社，竊先王之徽號，備中國之禮容，驅駕英賢，窺窬天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the dark signs to open his palace, modeled the divine capital to build his altars, stole the fine titles of former kings, and equipped himself with the ritual forms of China, driving worthy men and looking covetously upon the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he read the dark heavens to open his palace, modeled the divine capital to build his altars, stole the august titles of former kings, and equipped himself with the ritual forms of China, driving worthy men and looking covetously upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 然其器識高爽，風骨魁奇，姚興睹之而醉心，宋祖聞之而動色。

translations.literal: Yet his capacity and insight were lofty and clear, his bearing and bone structure outstanding and strange; Yao Xing saw him and was intoxicated in heart, and Emperor Wu of Song heard of him and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his capacity and insight were lofty and clear, his bearing and bone structure outstanding and strange. Yao Xing saw him and was intoxicated in heart; Emperor Wu of Song heard of him and changed color.

sentences.zh: 豈陰山之韞異氣，不然何以致斯乎！

translations.literal: Was it that the Yin Mountains hid a strange vital force—if not, how could it have produced such a man!
translations.idiomatic: Did the Yin Mountains hide some strange vital force—if not, how could they have produced such a man!

sentences.zh: 雖雄略過人，而凶殘未革，飾非距諫，酷害朝臣，部內囂然，忠良捲舌。

translations.literal: Though his bold design surpassed other men, his fierce cruelty was not reformed; he adorned wrong and rejected remonstrance, cruelly harmed court ministers, and within his domain there was uproar as loyal and good men rolled up their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Though his bold design surpassed other men, his fierce cruelty was not reformed. He adorned wrong and rejected remonstrance, cruelly harmed court ministers, and within his domain there was uproar as loyal and good men rolled up their tongues.

sentences.zh: 滅亡之禍，宜在厥身，猶及其嗣，非不幸也。

translations.literal: The calamity of extinction ought to have fallen on his own person, yet it reached even his heirs—this was no undeserved fate.
translations.idiomatic: The calamity of extinction ought to have fallen on his own person, yet it reached even his heirs—this was no undeserved fate.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：淳維遠裔，名王之餘。

translations.literal: The praise says: Chunwei, distant descendant, remnant of a named king.
translations.idiomatic: The praise says: Chunwei, distant descendant, remnant of a named king.

sentences.zh: 嘯群龍漠，乘釁侵漁。

translations.literal: Roaring with the dragon hosts in the desert, he seized the opening to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Roaring with the dragon hosts in the desert, he seized the opening to raid and plunder.

sentences.zh: 爰創宮宇，易彼氈廬。

translations.literal: Then he created palace halls and changed those felt tents.
translations.idiomatic: Then he created palace halls and changed those felt tents.

sentences.zh: 雖弄神器，猶曰凶渠。

translations.literal: Though he wielded the sacred regalia, he was still called a vicious chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held the throne, men still named him a murderous bandit.
